title: Part One: Induction and Adjustments
coreMove: Name shock as survival narrowing before you mistake its first bargain for truth.
sourcePressure: The early camp material centers on arrival at Auschwitz, shock, selection, delusion of reprieve, filth, mass bunks, beatings, suicidal thinking, and the first brutal adjustments.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Do not make this a lesson about adapting to change. The point is that shock compresses perception and produces desperate bargaining stories that may protect a person briefly while distorting judgment.

sourceAnchors.name: Auschwitz
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen source says the first phase begins with the crowded train ride to Auschwitz, where many arrivals are immediately sent to the gas chambers.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Auschwitz marks the collapse of ordinary expectation before any later lesson can be spoken.

sourceAnchors.name: delusion of reprieve
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar identifies the delusion of reprieve as part of early camp psychology.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The mind may tell a safer story for a few minutes because the true one is too large to hold.

sourceAnchors.name: selection
sourceAnchors.detail: The frozen support notes that arrival and selection destroy ordinary expectations quickly.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Selection should be treated as the visible moment when ordinary planning loses authority.

hook: Crisis reveals who you really are
counterintuition: The first reaction is not the true reaction
tryThisNow: Notice your emotions for sixty seconds

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: wildfire evacuation center intake when families arrive without addresses, medicine, or certainty
exampleSpecs.audience: a Red Cross intake lead trying to triage needs while everyone keeps asking whether the town is still standing
exampleSpecs.stakes: the first stories people tell themselves may determine whether insulin, pets, or missing relatives are recorded accurately
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she separates rumor from record by taping three columns to the folding table: confirmed, feared, unknown, then makes each family place its sentence in one column
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Ash falls from a jacket sleeve onto the intake form.

exampleSpecs.domain: financial fraud hotline after retirees discover accounts were emptied overnight
exampleSpecs.audience: a caseworker hearing callers bargain with impossible explanations
exampleSpecs.stakes: wrong first actions can erase records or expose people to a second scam
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he stops one caller from wiring recovery fees by asking her to read the bank timestamp aloud and label the hope as shock, not evidence
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Maybe the bank can reverse it if I pay the recovery fee," she says.

exampleSpecs.domain: factory layoff gate where workers are told their badges no longer open the turnstile
exampleSpecs.audience: an operations manager responsible for the first thirty minutes after an abrupt closure notice
exampleSpecs.stakes: people may sign bad paperwork while stunned because the familiar building no longer recognizes them
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the manager moves the severance forms away from the turnstile and gives workers a separate room before signatures begin
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The turnstile clicks red for the third badge in a row.

exampleSpecs.domain: oncology clinic first diagnosis visit when a family hears only one word after the scan result
exampleSpecs.audience: a nurse navigator watching a family nod while absorbing almost nothing
exampleSpecs.stakes: treatment consent can become theater if shock has blocked comprehension
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: it takes one failed teach-back for her to replace the packet with a single card: diagnosis, next appointment, who to call tonight
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Lea one silent elevator ride to see the packet had become a wall.

exampleSpecs.domain: airport repatriation desk after a sudden border closure leaves exchange students stranded
exampleSpecs.audience: a consular volunteer sorting panic from actionable information
exampleSpecs.stakes: students repeating hopeful rumors may miss the one bus that is actually confirmed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he asks each student to predict which rumor will still be true in two hours, then pins only confirmed transport to the board
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which sentence will still be true when the battery dies?

exampleSpecs.domain: search-and-rescue cold-water training when a trainee freezes after entering the lake
exampleSpecs.audience: an instructor teaching that shock is a body event before it is a character verdict
exampleSpecs.stakes: a trainee may misread panic as cowardice and quit the skill that could save someone later
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: you watch the instructor replay the first ninety seconds on a waterproof slate and mark each automatic gasp before discussing choices
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You hear the gasp before anyone says the water is cold.

skillTargets: identify shock-bargaining instead of treating it as reliable evidence
separate temporary adaptation from moral judgment
choose stabilizing actions that preserve facts under crisis

tryThisNowSpec: Write three columns on paper: confirmed, feared, unknown. Put one current worry into the right column before making the next decision.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
